title: Advanced Classical Syntax, Qur'anic Structures & Textual Iʿrāb

weeks.title: Unorthodox Verbs & The Relative Sentence (Jumlat al-Ṣilah)

chapters.title: Unorthodox & Invariable Verbs
chapters.rydingReference: Ryding Ch. 36 (Verbs of Being, Becoming, Seeming)
chapters.classicalFocus: Invariable verbs of praise and blame (niʿma, biʾsa), negative laysa, and verbs of appropinquation/hope (kāda, ʿasā).
coreRules: Laysa governs like kāna (nominative ism, accusative khabar); kāda and ʿasā govern imperfect complements.
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 59–60: rhetorical judgments and laysa/kāda clauses.

chapters.title: The Relative Sentence (Jumlat al-Ṣilah)
chapters.rydingReference: Ryding Ch. 14 (Relative Pronouns and Relative Clauses)
chapters.classicalFocus: Relative pronouns (al-mawṣūl: alladhī, allatī) for definite antecedents; asyndetic clauses for indefinite antecedents; returning resumptive pronoun (al-ʿāʾid).
coreRules: Definite antecedents require a relative pronoun; indefinite antecedents omit it.
The resumptive pronoun (al-ʿāʾid) links the relative clause back to the antecedent.
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 61–62: parsing relative clauses and resumptive pronouns in Qur'anic descriptions.

chapters.title: Conditionals & The Apodosis Connector (Fa-)
chapters.classicalFocus: Real conditions (in, idhā), counterfactual conditions (law, lawlā with la-), and fāʾ al-jazāʾ introducing non-verbal apodoses.
coreRules: Use fāʾ al-jazāʾ when the result clause is nominal, imperative, negated, or introduced by qad, sa-, sawfa, or lan.
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 63–64: identifying sharṭ, jazāʾ, and fāʾ al-jazāʾ in scriptural conditionals.

chapters.title: Cardinal Numbers, Time & Dates
chapters.classicalFocus: Chiastic gender polarity for 3–10; invariable compounds 11–19; decades 20–90; counted noun syntax (tamyīz al-ʿadad).
coreRules: 3–10 take plural genitive counted nouns with reverse gender; 11–99 take singular accusative; 100/1000 take singular genitive.
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 65–66: writing out numbers in classical texts and historical dates.

chapters.title: Ordinal Numbers & Fractions
chapters.classicalFocus: Ordinal numbers (al-aʿdād al-tartībiyyah) behaving as descriptive adjectives, and classical fractions.
coreRules: Ordinals agree with their noun in gender, case, and definiteness.
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 67–68: ordinal sequences and fractions.

chapters.title: Structure of Arabic Noun Forms
chapters.textbookTitle: The Structure of Arabic Noun Forms
chapters.classicalFocus: Primitive nouns (asmāʾ jāmidah) vs. derived substantives (mushtaqqāt); Form I maṣdar patterns (faʿl, fuʿūl, fiʿālah).
coreRules: Form I maṣādir are lexical and must be learned by pattern/dictionary.
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 69–70: classifying noun patterns and maṣādir.

chapters.title: Nouns of Place, Time, Instrument & Diminutives
chapters.textbookTitle: Noun Forms. The Noun of Place and Time. The Noun of Instrument. The Diminutive
chapters.rydingReference: Ryding Ch. 5 (Nouns of Place/Time, Instrument, Diminutive)
chapters.classicalFocus: Mafʿal/mafʿil (place/time), mifʿāl/mifʿal/mifʿalah (instrument), and fuʿayl/fuʿayʿil (diminutive).
coreRules: Nouns of place and time follow mafʿal or mafʿil according to imperfect vowel or weak root class.
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 71–72: classifying nouns of place, instrument, and verbal nouns in Qur'anic passages.

chapters.title: Relative Adjectives (Al-Nisbah) & Intensive Forms
chapters.textbookTitle: The Relative Noun and Adjective. Various Adjectival Forms
chapters.rydingReference: Ryding Ch. 5 (§5.7, Nouns of Intensity) & Ch. 10 (Part Two, Adjective Derivation)
chapters.classicalFocus: Nisbah adjectives (-īy) and intensive adjective patterns (ṣiyagh al-mubālaghah: faʿʿāl, faʿūl, miʿfāl) frequent in divine attributes.
coreRules: Forming the nisbah removes tāʾ marbūṭah and suffixes -iyyun / -iyyatun.
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 73–74: parsing al-Asmāʾ al-Ḥusnā and intensive patterns.

chapters.title: Abstract Nouns & Classical Proper Names
chapters.classicalFocus: Abstract nouns (-iyyah) and classical name structure (ism, kunya, nasab, laqab).
coreRules: Classical biographical names distinguish ism, kunya (Abū/Umm), nasab (ibn/bint), and laqab.
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 75–76: analyzing classical patronymics.

chapters.title: Exceptional Gender Categories
chapters.classicalFocus: Unmarked feminine nouns (paired body parts, elemental nouns, cities/tribes) and common-gender nouns.
coreRules: Paired body parts and many elemental nouns (shams, nār, arḍ) are grammatically feminine without markers.
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 77–78: identifying unmarked feminines.

chapters.title: Plurals of Paucity, Multitude & Plural of Plurals
chapters.classicalFocus: Plurals of paucity (jamʿ al-qillah, 3–10) vs. multitude (jamʿ al-kathrah), plural of plurals (jamʿ al-jamʿ), and collective nouns.
coreRules: Four patterns (afʿul, afʿāl, afʿilah, fiʿlah) classically denote paucity (3–10).
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 79–80: classifying rare plurals.

chapters.title: Diptote Declension (Al-Mamnūʿ min al-Ṣarf)
chapters.rydingReference: Ryding Ch. 8 (§8.5, Diptotes: Al-Mamnūʿ min al-Ṣarf)
chapters.classicalFocus: Nouns barred from tanwīn taking two endings (-u nom., -a acc./gen.); causes (foreign names, feminine/alif-nūn names, afʿal, mafāʿil/mafāʿīl); reversion rule.
coreRules: Diptotes revert to full three-case triptote declension (taking kasrah in the genitive) when prefixed by al- or serving as muḍāf.
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 81–82: vocalizing diptotes in scriptural text.

chapters.title: Comprehensive Accusative Syntax (Al-Manṣūbāt)
chapters.rydingReference: Ryding Ch. 8 (§8.3, Accusative Functions) & Ch. 11 (Adverbial Accusatives)
chapters.classicalFocus: Direct object (mafʿūl bihi), absolute cognate accusative (mafʿūl muṭlaq), circumstantial accusative (ḥāl), specification (tamyīz), and cause/purpose (mafʿūl li-ajlihi).
coreRules: Ḥāl is an indefinite accusative participle/adjective describing the state of a definite antecedent during an action.
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 83–84: identifying and vocalizing ḥāl, tamyīz, and mafʿūl muṭlaq in Qur'anic prose.

chapters.title: The Permutative / Apposition (Al-Badal)
chapters.classicalFocus: Apposition types: identical replacement, part-of-whole, and inclusive quality; case agreement.
coreRules: The badal takes the exact same grammatical case as its antecedent.
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 85–86: parsing classical titles and appositives.

chapters.title: Prepositions & Locative Semi-Prepositions (Ẓurūf)
chapters.classicalFocus: True prepositions (ḥurūf al-jarr) vs. locative/temporal semi-prepositions (ẓurūf); idiomatic verb–preposition pairs.
coreRules: Prepositional choice can alter a verb's meaning (e.g., raghiba fī vs. raghiba ʿan).
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 87–88: parsing prepositional idioms.

chapters.title: Adverbial Usages & Inna wa-Akhawātuhā
chapters.textbookTitle: Adverbial Usages, including miscellaneous quasi-adverbial particles
chapters.classicalFocus: Corroborating particles (inna, anna, ka-anna, lākinna, layta, laʿalla) and al-lām al-muzahlaqah.
coreRules: Inna induces its subject (ism inna) into the accusative while its predicate (khabar inna) remains nominative.
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 89–90: parsing emphatic sentences introduced by inna.

chapters.title: Coordinating Conjunctions (Ḥurūf al-ʿAṭf)
chapters.classicalFocus: Semantic nuances of wa- (simple link), fa- (immediate consequence), thumma (delayed consequence), and bal (rectification).
coreRules: Conjoined elements share the grammatical case or mood of their antecedent.
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 91–92: conjunction nuances.

chapters.title: Oaths & Interjections
chapters.classicalFocus: Oath particles (wāw, tāʾ, bāʾ al-qasam) governing the genitive; classical interjections.
coreRules: Oath particles govern the object sworn by in the genitive case (e.g., wa-llāhi).
chapters.practiceFocus: Parsing classical oath formulas and interjections.

chapters.title: Exception (Al-Istithnāʾ)
chapters.classicalFocus: Syntax of illā across positive, complete negative, and defective negative clauses; ghayr and siwā.
coreRules: After illā: positive clauses take accusative; defective negative clauses take the verb-governed case; ghayr/siwā govern the genitive.
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 93–94: analyzing exceptions in theological covenants.

weeks.title: Classical Versification Metrics & Capstone Qur'anic Analysis

chapters.title: Classical Versification Metrics (Al-ʿArūḍ)
chapters.rydingReference: Ryding Appendix II (Glossary of Arabic Linguistic Terminology)
chapters.classicalFocus: Metrical system of al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad: cords (sabab), pegs (watad), and classical meters (al-Ṭawīl, al-Kāmil, al-Basīṭ, al-Wāfir).
coreRules: Prosodic scansion maps long and short syllables into recurring feet (tafʿīlāt).
chapters.practiceFocus: Scanning classical hemistichs and vocalizing rhyme consonants.

chapters.title: Capstone Qur'anic & Classical Literary Analysis
chapters.textbookTitle: Supplement. (Specimens from Arabic Literature) & Appendix B
chapters.rydingReference: Ryding Appendix II & Full Morphosyntactic Reference
chapters.classicalFocus: Word-by-word iʿrāb of Sūrat al-Fātiḥah and Qur'anic selections; unvocalized readings from Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Kalīlah wa-Dimnah, and Ibn Baṭṭūṭah; Appendix B reference transition.
coreRules: Apply the 3-step Iʿrāb Parsing Routine before translating, keeping grammatical analysis distinct from tafsīr.
chapters.practiceFocus: Capstone reading and word-by-word syntactic analysis of authentic classical texts.
